subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is meant by primary processing of food?
options: Converting raw materials (such as harvested crops or animals) into food commodities that can be eaten or used as ingredients
Adding preservatives and colourings to a finished product before sale
Combining several ready-made ingredients into a complete meal
Reheating a manufactured product so that it is ready to serve
questions.explain: Primary processing turns a raw agricultural material into a basic commodity or ingredient, such as milling grain or slaughtering animals.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of PRIMARY processing?
options: Milling wheat grain into flour
Baking flour into bread
Turning milk into yoghurt
Making tomatoes into pasta sauce
questions.explain: Milling wheat into flour changes a raw material into a basic commodity, which is primary processing.

questions.q: What is meant by secondary processing of food?
options: Turning a primary-processed food into another food product
Growing and harvesting a raw crop from the land
Slaughtering an animal to produce meat
Extracting oil by pressing seeds
questions.explain: Secondary processing takes a primary product (like flour or milk) and converts it into a further product such as bread or cheese.

questions.q: Which vitamin is most easily destroyed by heat during cooking and processing?
options: Vitamin C
Vitamin A
Vitamin D
Vitamin K
questions.explain: Vitamin C is water-soluble and heat-sensitive, so it is readily lost during cooking and processing.

questions.q: Which group of vitamins is most likely to be lost by leaching into cooking water?
options: The water-soluble B and C vitamins
The fat-soluble A and D vitamins
The fat-soluble E and K vitamins
All vitamins are equally likely to leach
questions.explain: Because B and C vitamins dissolve in water, they leach out into cooking liquid that is then discarded.

questions.q: Which statement best describes organic food production?
options: Food produced without artificial pesticides, fertilisers or routine use of drugs
Food produced using the maximum possible artificial inputs to raise yield
Food that has been genetically modified for higher yield
Food produced entirely inside heated factory units
questions.explain: Organic production avoids artificial pesticides and fertilisers and restricts routine drug use, relying on natural methods.

questions.q: What does the term 'free-range' indicate about how animals such as hens are kept?
options: The animals have access to open-air outdoor areas rather than being confined
The animals are kept permanently indoors in high-density cages
The animals are fed only genetically modified feed
The animals are reared entirely without any human care
questions.explain: Free-range systems allow animals regular access to the outdoors, unlike intensive caged systems.

questions.q: A dairy takes fresh milk and turns it into cheese. How is this best classified?
options: Secondary processing, because a primary product is made into a new product
Primary processing, because milk is a raw agricultural material
Not a form of processing at all
Primary processing, because no heat is used
questions.explain: Milk is a primary product, so converting it into cheese is a secondary processing stage.

questions.q: Why is producing sugar from sugar beet described as primary processing?
options: It converts a raw harvested crop into a basic food commodity
It combines several finished ingredients into a meal
It reheats an already-manufactured product
It only involves packaging an existing product
questions.explain: Extracting sugar from the raw beet crop turns a raw material into a usable commodity, which is primary processing.

questions.q: Why does boiling green vegetables in a large volume of water reduce their vitamin C content so much?
options: Vitamin C is destroyed by heat and also leaches into the cooking water
Vitamin C is converted into fibre during boiling
The water adds extra vitamin C that masks the loss
Boiling increases the vitamin C so none is lost
questions.explain: Both heat destruction and leaching into the discarded water reduce the vitamin C in boiled vegetables.

questions.q: Compared with vitamin C, why are the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K generally better retained during cooking?
options: They are more stable to heat and do not dissolve into cooking water
They are destroyed more quickly by heat
They evaporate from the food during cooking
They dissolve readily into cooking water and are lost
questions.explain: Fat-soluble vitamins resist heat and, being insoluble in water, are not leached away during boiling.

questions.q: White flour is required by UK law to have certain nutrients added back after milling. Why is this fortification needed?
options: Milling removes the bran and germ, lowering the fibre, iron and B vitamins
Milling adds too much fat that must be balanced out
White flour naturally contains no protein at all
Fortification is done only to improve the flour's colour
questions.explain: Removing the bran and germ during milling reduces nutrients, so calcium, iron, thiamin and niacin are added back by law.

questions.q: Which is a recognised advantage of intensive (conventional large-scale) food production?
options: It can produce large quantities of food at a lower cost to the consumer
It always improves animal welfare compared with free-range systems
It never uses any artificial fertilisers or pesticides
It guarantees higher nutritional value than organic food
questions.explain: Intensive production maximises output and keeps prices low, though it can raise welfare and environmental concerns.

questions.q: Why is organic food usually more expensive for the consumer than conventionally produced food?
options: Yields are often lower and production is more labour-intensive
It is transported over much shorter distances
It requires no land or farming at all
It is always genetically modified to reduce costs
questions.explain: Lower yields and higher labour and input costs of organic methods raise the price paid by consumers.

questions.q: A student wants to cook broccoli while keeping as much vitamin C as possible. Which method should they choose?
options: Steam it lightly for a short time
Boil it in plenty of water for a long time
Simmer it slowly in a large uncovered pan
Boil it, then keep it hot for an hour before serving
questions.explain: Short steaming limits both heat exposure and leaching, retaining more of the heat-sensitive vitamin C.

questions.q: A bakery buys in flour, then uses it to produce loaves of bread. Which stage of processing is the bakery carrying out?
options: Secondary processing
Primary processing
No processing takes place
Primary processing followed by harvesting
questions.explain: The bakery converts the primary product (flour) into a new product (bread), which is secondary processing.

questions.q: A cook wants to reduce the loss of B vitamins when preparing potatoes. Which action would help most?
options: Cook the potatoes in their skins and use only a little water
Peel and cut them small, then boil for a long time in lots of water
Soak the cut potatoes in water for several hours first
Boil them and pour the cooking water down the sink
questions.explain: Cooking in the skin with minimal water reduces the surface area exposed and limits leaching of water-soluble B vitamins.

questions.q: A shopper wants eggs from hens that have had access to the outdoors and are willing to pay a little more. Which label should they look for?
options: Free-range
Caged
Genetically modified
Ultra-processed
questions.explain: Free-range eggs come from hens given outdoor access, matching the shopper's welfare preference.
